record.title: Rosso international ferry suspension during pirogue operators’ protest, 5 April 2021
record.scope: Rosso ferry service across the Senegal River between Mauritania and Senegal
record.direction: Cross-river ferry service reported stopped; directional passenger/vehicle impacts not separately quantified.
record.movement: Users of the international ferry service; passenger, vehicle and goods composition not separately established.
record.exceptions: No exemption during the temporary ferry stoppage established. Broader small-boat ban remained a separate issue.
record.imposing_authority: Senegalese authorities requested suspension from Mauritanian authorities; reported by Sahara Medias
record.enforcement: Correspondent reports traffic stopped and resumed, alongside the attributed authority request.
record.relationship: Distinct protest-related ferry interruption under the wider COVID restrictions; related to W-023 and promoted from preserved lead R15-AN-L001 after separate event review.
record.status_observation: Same-evening resumption reported in the contemporary 5 April 2021 article; no present-status inference.
record.official_rationale: Reported official request to stop the ferry until the authorized pirogue-operator protest ended; no separate security rationale stated.
record.context: Protest concerned continued COVID-era prohibition of small-boat activity. The temporary ferry interruption is a distinct local phase, not the onset or end of the wider pandemic restriction.
record.uncertainty: Exact clock times, category-level exemptions and individual implementation observations are unspecified. Reported five-hour interruption is not converted into a calculated duration.

historical.duration_note: Short same-day ferry episode; no calculated interval in proposal

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Correspondent describes stopped then resumed cross-river traffic, together with the authority request; this is more than a planned notice.
Article dated Monday 5 April 2021 says interruption preceded resumption that evening. Exact start clock time unknown; day supported by same-day account.
Both language versions describe resumed traffic that Monday evening; endpoint applies to ferry service only, not all Rosso boat categories.

Hierarchical coding: see Rationale coding for subcategories, attribution and phases. The health-policy and livelihood codes describe the pirogue operators' grievance and the protest context. The official ferry-suspension motive beyond waiting for the protest to end is not separately established. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): Immediate trigger is authority-requested suspension during authorized protest. Public health is background to protesters’ grievance; no rationale code assigned to this separate stoppage.
International Rosso ferry stopped; pirogue ban and national frontier policy are separate. Categories and directional implementation not resolved.
Report characterizes a single short interruption and resumption. Minute-level continuity and exemptions are not independently established; no interval calculated.
